item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This was entertaining in places, although it dragged a bit overall. There are a lot of sections like this:

He broke from his standing position by the door exactly two and a half seconds behind schedule, lengthening his strides to make up for time lost contemplating the decor.

and

Dark held his bleeding nose with one hand and took a swing at his assailant, his rifle swinging through a shelf of ancient tomes with the unintended momentum

— that are unnecessarily verbose, and read like a very initial draft. Your descriptive prose is almost laborious, and weighted with phrases that— while acceptable on their own— make for sloggy reading when pasted together. That's one of my own biggest faults, so I'm especially wary of it when I read. I'm not hugely invested in any MC&D headcanon, so I think the last line is great and the whole of the story has some potential— it is just feels very paint-by-numbers as it is now.

Also, that comma in the title is driving me mad.

item.content:encoded:
I like the concept. The misters M, C, and D must have paid the bills somehow before their clubs reputation was established; and art-raiding commandos seems like a more interesting origin story than most.

But there would have to be some sort of explanation for the time discrepancy before I'd accept this as headcanon. How is MC&D the organization such a well-established traditional institution if MC&D the men were (not so) petty thieves so recently?
